articles.title: Mice That Sing? Tiny Throat Balloons Make Their Wild Tunes!
articles.summary: Alston's singing mice inflate tiny balloon-like sacs in their throats to belt out 100 notes in just 10 seconds. Scientists blocked the sacs and the songs stopped—proving the balloons are the secret to their speedy serenades.

articles.title: Venus Is Putting On a Double Sky Show This July—Here's How to Watch!
articles.summary: Venus will cozy up to the bright star Regulus on July 9, then meet a thin crescent moon on July 17. Look low in the west after sunset—binoculars will make the view even cooler.

articles.title: Hubble Snaps a Sparkly Star Nursery That Looks Like Fireworks!
articles.summary: NASA's Hubble telescope captured LH 95, a star-forming region with glowing red gas and brilliant blue stars. It holds 2,500 baby stars still growing, plus a giant star 60 times heavier than the Sun.
